summary: All 41 occurrences checked. II mʕazam- and III maʕzam- coexist with the same invitation meaning; preserve both paradigms and inherited variant spellings. Only the empty duplicate II block is consolidated.
Invitees occur as zero-marked nouns, suffixes, and reciprocal ḥḏoḏe. Preterit can have an l-marked lexical agent (11/299; PrS 16/14); destination l- and meal ʕal- are different roles.

Invited status is Detransitive Part. Pass.; plural addressees and an unexpressed inviter do not create an additional invitation sense. The nominal ʕezomo is already present as Nomen Actionis, so the reader’s Infinitiv novelty claim is rejected.
Apparent m loss/contraction in maʕəzlux, maʕəzla, gmaʕaznox and related forms is retained verbatim. No emendation into ʕzl is justified by an invitation context.

The I stem proposal relies on two independent source shapes, ʕzəmle and kʕozəm, particularly the o-vowel Infectum; it is not based on a single clipped m-less token. Do not infer unattested forms or collapse II/III into I.

ʕəzmənxu, ʕzəmmallox and ʕƏzmiwolox remain uncertain in stem or suffix segmentation. Food at a wedding or invitation to eat does not establish a separate lexical serving sense, as round 1 already noted.
Preterit-wa III maʕzamlewolan contains the agent-series form and past suffix with recipient -lan. The English had been invited does not justify Detransitive.
Round-1 consolidation of duplicate II and repair of the invitation clause/Nomen Actionis remain in force and are not repeated as new corrections.
Confirm II assignment of unprefixed ʕazəm/ʕazeme against a reduced III alternative. III’s inherited Imperativ has maʕzəm; no arbitrary m is restored.
Check first-person segmentation of gmaʕəzalle/gmaʕəzallox and contraction in Maʕəzlux/Maʕəzla, and II versus III in PrS 16/15 Maʕazamla.
Is mazʕminawole at 11/252 metathesis or a text error? Keep the inherited maʕzəmina-wo-le and source form visible pending edition check.
100/29 is partially aligned and marks a clause unverständlich. Neither token’s translation is quoted; obtain a complete aligned version before adding the reciprocal example.
The inherited II note 1) inviting, invitation pertains to Nomen Actionis, not invited people. Confirm editorial section placement while retaining inherited text.
Confirm I ʕzəmle/ʕozəm against m-loss/contraction of II or III, using Jan 1.2/36 and 3.14/127 together. The source-specific new stem is machine-proposed.
How should ʕəzmənxu (1.38/1660), ʕzəmmallox (2.4/698) and ʕƏzmiwolox (2.5/1340) be segmented and assigned? The first persons/voice are not inferred from the machine translation.

rationale: The imperative of 'schneiden' is 'schneide'; the cited edition reads 'Schneide schnell'.

summary: Whole city denotes invited inhabitants. Reciprocal ḥḏoḏe is an overt active object, not Detransitive; self-invitation in 63/31 is pragmatic.
Inviting to a meal entails hosting/feeding in PrS 16/13–15, 73/25 and 82/3,8; this does not by itself require a distinct bewirten sense.
Jan retains the already recognized invitation/hosting range, with destination l- and invited people from multiple towns; no distinct bewirten sense.
